ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A coal block (which can be regarded as a particle) is placed on a horizontal light-colored long conveyor belt. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the coal block and the conveyor belt is $\upmu = 0.2$. Initially, both the conveyor belt and the coal block are at rest. The conveyor belt is then made to move with a constant acceleration of $\scriptstyle\mathbf{a}_{0}=4\mathbf{m}/\mathbf{s}^{2}$. Once its velocity reaches $\scriptstyle\mathbf{v}_{0}=8\ensuremath{\mathbf{m}}/\mathbf{s}$, it continues at this constant velocity. After some time, a black mark is left on the conveyor belt, after which the coal block no longer slides relative to the conveyor belt.

1. Determine the length of this black mark.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A coal block (which can be regarded as a particle) is placed on a horizontal light-colored long conveyor belt. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the coal block and the conveyor belt is $\mu = 0.2$. Initially, both the conveyor belt and the coal block are at rest. The conveyor belt is then made to move with a constant acceleration of $a_0 = 4\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$. Once its velocity reaches $v_0 = 8\,\mathrm{m/s}$, it continues at this constant velocity. After some time, a black mark is left on the conveyor belt, after which the coal block no longer slides relative to the conveyor belt. Determine the length of this black mark.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: This is a text-only physics problem, so no image evidence is needed. Take g ≈ 10 m/s^2. While the coal block is sliding on the belt, the only horizontal force on it is kinetic friction, so its acceleration is a_c = μg = 0.2 × 10 = 2 m/s^2 in the belt's direction. First stage: the conveyor belt accelerates from rest at a_0 = 4 m/s^2 until it reaches v_0 = 8 m/s. The time is t_1 = v_0/a_0 = 8/4 = 2 s. In this time, the belt displacement is s_b1 = (1/2)a_0 t_1^2 = (1/2)×4×2^2 = 8 m. The coal displacement is s_c1 = (1/2)a_c t_1^2 = (1/2)×2×2^2 = 4 m. At the end of this stage, the belt speed is 8 m/s, while the coal speed is v_c1 = a_c t_1 = 2×2 = 4 m/s, so the coal is still sliding relative to the belt. Second stage: the belt moves uniformly at 8 m/s, while the coal continues accelerating at 2 m/s^2 until its speed also reaches 8 m/s. The required time is t_2 = (8 - 4)/2 = 2 s. In this time, the belt displacement is s_b2 = 8t_2 = 16 m. The coal displacement is s_c2 = 4t_2 + (1/2)a_c t_2^2 = 4×2 + (1/2)×2×2^2 = 8 + 4 = 12 m. The black mark length equals the total relative sliding distance between belt and coal before relative motion stops. Since the belt remains ahead of the coal throughout, this is (s_b1 + s_b2) - (s_c1 + s_c2) = (8 + 16) - (4 + 12) = 8 m.
